title: First recordings in Berlin through acoustic horns
summary: The recording people came after four or five days; the drums were placed in the hall and the band played into horns, recording show numbers.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: And during that time -- it was during this time that you recorded for Polydor, wasn't it?
No, who did we record for? No, it wasn't Polydor. // I think I did record later for Polydor, but this wasn't Polydor.
But the first recordings were no --
First wasn't Polydor. Anyhow, we had been there about four or five days and then come the people from the recording company, and said, 'Look, we would like for you to record.'
Okay, so that was Vox that you made those first recordings for in Berlin.

Well this was really a hassle. First we had to decide which of the numbers it was good to record. And another thing we was bothered with at that time was the mikes. We had been so used to having the drum. Now the drummer sat out in the hall and we had to play, we'd just feel what we wanted. And we got some feeling from him, but they didn't record the drum.
Were these microphones or horns at that time?
They were horns.
They were horns, right.
Yeah, there wasn't no mikes at all. It was before the day of the mike.
Uh hunh. So this was before the electric recordings.
Yes. The megaphones, or some kind of horns. The boys played through the horns.
Yeah, horns. So they had to put the drums far away, otherwise they would distort the sound.
That was exactly what it was.
And that made it difficult for you.
Yeah, it was very difficult. And you had to be very true with what you was trying to do as far as you could. Otherwise you had nothing to skate on.
Uh hunh.
Your drum would cover a multitude of sins. But everything had to be true.
But the numbers you recorded, were they all taken from the show?
No.
I notice you did about --
Our specialties, some of them. And then others, like "Alabamy Bound". And we did others, like, "Shanghai Shuffle", and -- "Minnetonka" was our opening...
"By the Waters of the Minnetonka".
And some others we did we had done on the
show, because they had asked for those.
So those would be -- the way they would be on the record would be the exact same arrangement --
Yeah, that we played on the show.
Right.

And so we were doing very well with that. We had made two takes with them and was enjoying ourselves, that's the main thing. And rehearsing. And then riding around and seeing Berlin. There was much to see. The Grunewald, where there was beautiful mansions and all, places, things that we had never seen. Because, you see, Chris, here in America, our home and our paradise and everything was Harlem.
Right. And this was a different world.

Now, we had never seen all these things before. And during the war, I had never seen them, the boys had seen less than I. But during the war, everything was blown down by the Germans. And so the places that were beautiful, we didn't know nothing about -- so now, we're getting a chance of seeing a place like Berlin. And then the people were so much nicer to you. Everybody was very fine and we really enjoyed ourself there. We've got to say that much.
